title: Entropion: Diagnosis & Management
summary: A comprehensive clinical guide to the evaluation and management of entropion, distinguishing between involutional, cicatricial, and spastic etiologies to guide surgical intervention. This poster covers the complete workup from history to complex eyelid reconstruction techniques.

sections.title: Clinical Case Presentation
sections.content: A 62-year-old woman reports that her right eye has been irritated, red, and tearing for months. Artificial tears help briefly but do not really alleviate the scratchy sensation she experiences.

rows: Hx of previous surgical or accidental trauma
Hx of chemical injuries, OCP, SJS, trachoma
Misdirected lashes hitting the globe without lid margin inversion.
Extra row of lashes arising from meibomian gland orifices.
Extra skin fold pushing lashes against eye; common in Asians/infants.
Outward turning of the lid margin (opposite of entropion).
Inflammation of lid margins; no lid malposition.

branches: Elicitation: Ask patient to squeeze eyes (Intermittent Entropion)
Lid Excursion: Look for decreased excursion of lower lid in downgaze (Involutional)
Laxity Testing: Eyelid Distraction & Snap Tests
Manual Repositioning: Check for resistance vs easy return
Conjunctival Check: Fornix shortening or scarring (Cicatricial)

rows: Lid returns to normal position with finger and remains for a blink or two/squeezing.
Manually pull lower eyelid away; abnormal if >6 mm off the eyeball.
Pull lid inferiorly; abnormal if it doesn't spring back without a blink.
Resistance when trying to return lid to normal; returns to inverted position immediately.

branches: Involutional: Transverse everting sutures (temporary), Jones Procedure, Wies Procedure
Horizontal Shortening: Lateral Tarsal Strip (LTS), Wedge Excision, Kuhnt-Szymanowski
Cicatricial: Tarsal fracture (tarsotomy), Terminal tarsal rotation, Mucous membrane grafts
Spastic: Treat underlying irritation, Quickert sutures if irritation persists

content.explanation: Factors for Involutional Entropion: H - Horizontal lid laxity; A - Attenuation or disinsertion of lower lid retractors; R - Retrapalpebral/Orbicularis 'Ride-over'; D - Degeneration of tarsal plate.

sections.title: Urgent Red Flags
content: Corneal Ulceration or Perforation due to lash rub

sections.title: Clinical Pearls
content: The Jones procedure involves reinserting the lower lid retractors to the inferior tarsal border.
Wies procedure is a full-thickness transverse blepharotomy with everting sutures.
Terminal tarsal rotation is specifically indicated for upper eyelid cicatricial entropion.
Always treat the underlying cause of spastic entropion (e.g., inflammation, infection) before committing to permanent surgery.
